precepts.text: For the tidings, because it cometh: every heart shall melt, all hands shall be feeble, every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall be weak as water.
precepts.point: Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: the Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“For the tidings; because it cometh: and every heart shall melt, and all hands shall be feeble, and every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall be weak as water: behold, it cometh, and shall be brought to pass, saith the Lord God.” Every heart melting, every spirit fainting, knees weak as water: this is the Lord's doing, and he says it shall be brought to pass.

That is what the people of Israel felt after Ai, their hearts melted and became as water. The Lord controls the heart of the fight, not the sword; if we are not spiritually right with him, he will make us lose.

precepts.why: Nebuchadnezzar deciding whether to destroy the Israelites or the Ammonites first: “For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination”: to use witchcraft. “He looked in the liver.” Nebuchadnezzar was heavy into what we call today voodoo.

moments.label: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: The Third Kingdom of Babylon

points: The word of the Most High comes to Ezekiel to set his face toward Jerusalem, drop his word toward the holy places, and prophesy against the land of Israel.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: The Most High is against her and will draw forth His sword out of his sheath to cut off the righteous and the wicked, the sword being the nations He sends.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: He judges us as a nation, so the righteous and the wicked all get judged together; the sword goes forth against all flesh from the south to the north and shall not return.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: Ezekiel is told to sigh with the breaking of his loins and with bitterness before their eyes.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: When they ask why he sighs he is to answer that it is for the tidings that come, because every heart shall melt, all hands be feeble, every spirit faint, and all knees be weak as water.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: A sword is sharpened and furbished, meaning polished, sharpened to make a sore slaughter and furbished that it may glitter.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: It contemneth the rod of His son, and Judah is that rod; the sword is given to be furbished into the hand of the slayer.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: Ezekiel is to cry and howl, for the sword shall be upon His people and upon all the princes of Israel; it is a trial, a sword that has already been tested by other nations that the Lord uses.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: Ezekiel is to smite his hands together and let the sword be doubled the third time, the sword of the slain that enters even into their private chambers so there is no escape.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: The point of the sword is set against all their gates, and that point is Babylon pointing at all the gates of Jerusalem.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: The sword goes one way or the other, to the right hand or the left, whichever way it turns to seek judgment and destruction upon Jerusalem, and the Most High's fury shall rest there.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: The word of the Most High comes again to appoint two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come, both out of one land.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: One way points to Rabbath of the Ammonites and the other to Judah in fenced Jerusalem, and the king of Babylon stands at the parting of the ways to use divination, which is witchcraft.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: He makes his arrows bright, consults with images, and looks in the liver, and at his right hand the divination points for Jerusalem to appoint captains and set battering rams against the gates.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: Because their iniquity is remembered and their transgressions discovered so that their sins appear, they shall be taken with the hand.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: To the profane wicked prince of Israel whose day is come, He says remove the diadem and take off the crown, exalt him that is low and abase him that is high.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: He will overturn, overturn, overturn it, and it shall be no more until he come whose right it is, and He will give it to him.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: Concerning the Ammonites and their reproach, the sword is drawn and furbished to consume because of the glittering.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: While the diviners see vanity and divine a lie, the sword will bring them upon the necks of the slain whose day is come.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: He will judge them in the place where they were created, in the land of their nativity, pour out His indignation, blow against them in the fire of His wrath, and deliver them into the hand of brutish men skilful to destroy; they shall be for fuel to the fire and be no more remembered.

note.label: Ezekiel 21: The Sword of the Lord Is Drawn

points: Nebuchadnezzar used witchcraft too. “Appoint thee two ways, that the sword of the king of Babylon may come”, “choose it at the head of the way to the city”: Nebuchadnezzar had to choose a way, a kingdom to destroy and take over, “to Rabbath of the Ammonites, and to Judah in Jerusalem the defenced.”

note.label: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: The Third Kingdom of Babylon

points: Watch this: “For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination”. Nebuchadnezzar used divination; that’s another name for witchcraft. “He made his arrows bright, he consulted with images, he looked in the liver.” He consulted with images, meaning idols, and he looked in the liver.

Some of you that used to practice voodoo know about looking in the liver. They rip it out of a cow or a goat or a lamb; you look at the liver, you taste the liver, you roll bones on the ground. How many of you are from Haiti? From Jamaica? People want to be quiet when you ask them certain questions; nobody knows what you’re talking about. So he had images and he looked in the liver: that’s all witchcraft.

The word on the screen calls it ‘the inspection of the entrails of sacrificial victims’ (victims; I was trying to be nice and said animals), ‘and especially of the liver as a means of ascertaining the will of the gods’, a custom that ‘prevailed also in Babylonia’, the king ‘employing all these different kinds of divination to make sure of the proper path’.

note.label: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: The Third Kingdom of Babylon

points: “At his right hand was the divination for Jerusalem, to appoint captains”, “to appoint battering rams against the gates”. He consulted Satan, looking in the liver and looking at idols, to say who should I destroy first.

note.label: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: The Third Kingdom of Babylon

points: “And it shall be unto them as a false divination in their sight”: Israel said, I don’t worry about that. “But he will call to remembrance the iniquity, that they may be taken.” No, you’re going to be taken. The Lord let everything Nebuchadnezzar was doing work, because Israel, your time was over, you were going into slavery. And that’s exactly what happened to us.
